pages.text: Dingding came back from the paddy and reached for a rice cake in the basket with muddy hands. "Your hands!" Mom called, but Dingding did not stop.
Dingding ate quickly and went back to the paddy. Dirty fingerprints marked the white rice cake. Mom looked at them.
Later, Dingding's tummy gurgled and hurt. Dingding crouched down, holding their belly, with tears in their eyes.
Mr. Ming, who kept ducks in the lowest paddy, came into the yard. He looked at the soil on Dingding's hands and between the fingers.
"Ducks dip their beaks in water before a meal," he said, pointing to ducks rinsing their beaks. He sang, "Muddy Hands, Scrub in Water!"
Mom brought a basin of water and some soap. Dingding dipped their hands in. "One!" Cool water flowed around the fingers.
"Two!" Dingding rubbed up soapy bubbles. "Three!" Dingding scrubbed between the fingers. The water turned the color of mud.
Dingding rinsed. Their hands were clean, and all the mud was in the basin. Dingding sniffed. No muddy smell! "There was that much mud?"
The next day, Dingding went to the basin first. "Hands first, rice cake later!" Dingding repeated the three steps. Mr. Ming held up both hands.
Mom held Dingding's hand and kissed their cheek. "Your hands are cleaner than the basin now!" The mud stayed in the water. Dingding ate a rice cake with no tummy ache. "Muddy Hands, Scrub in Water!"
